primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic nephropathy with superimposed hypertensive nephrosclerosis (stage 5 CKD)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily, titrate up to 5-10 mg once daily over 4-6 weeks as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each titration
medications.purpose: Control hypertension, reduce proteinuria and provide renal protection
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line recommendation: ACE inhibitor for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 0.5 g (½ tablet) orally three times daily, titrate to maintain serum bicarbonate ≥22 mmol/L
medications.duration: Until serum bicarbonate ≥22 mmol/L, then review quarterly
medications.purpose: Correct metabolic acidosis associated with advanced CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises correction of metabolic acidosis in CKD stage 4‑5

medications.dose: 200 mg (equivalent to 65 mg elemental iron) orally once daily
medications.duration: Until ferritin >100 µg/L and transferrin saturation >20%, then review
medications.purpose: Treat iron‑deficiency anemia of CKD (pending iron studies)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends treating anaemia of CKD after iron deficiency is confirmed

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually; add if BP remains >140/90 mmHg after ACE‑I optimisation
medications.purpose: Additional blood pressure control if target not achieved with ACE‑I alone
medications.nice_justification: NG203 non‑pharmacological BP target <140/90 mmHg; CCB is recommended as add‑on therapy

contraindications.reason: eGFR 5.4 mL/min/1.73m² (<30) – high risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Insulin or GLP‑1 receptor agonist after specialist review

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention in advanced CKD
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury

contraindications.alternative: Avoid; consider alternative mood stabiliser if required

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m² – high risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy
contraindications.alternative: Use low‑osmolar contrast with pre‑hydration and prophylaxis if imaging unavoidable

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure reading not provided – assumed uncontrolled, hence ACE‑I initiation and possible CCB add‑on.
Baseline serum potassium not available – assume ≤5.0 mmol/L; will check 1‑2 weeks after starting Ramipril.
Baseline liver function tests not provided – assume normal; will obtain before starting Atorvastatin.
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) not available – oral iron prescribed pending results.
Allergy status unknown – will verify before initiating any medication.
treatment_summary: Initiate ACE‑I (Ramipril) and statin (Atorvastatin) as first‑line therapy for CKD with proteinuria and cardiovascular risk. Correct metabolic acidosis with oral sodium bicarbonate. Address possible iron‑deficiency anaemia with ferrous sulfate after labs. Add amlodipine if blood pressure remains above target. All choices follow NICE NG203, avoid contraindicated drugs, and include monitoring plans for renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, and bicarbonate levels.
